content: 1. Individuals living with HIV who also have drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB) require further research to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of newer antiretroviral (ARV) drugs used in first-line, second-line, or third-line treatment regimens in the context of TB and HIV co-infection. 2. Additional data is necessary to assess the use of corticosteroids in people living with HIV who have low CD4 cell counts, specifically to prevent immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). 3. There is a need for improved long-term data on the suppression of viral loads in individuals using formulations containing efavirenz 400 mg, particularly among pregnant women and those requiring co-treatment for TB, especially when rifampicin is included. 4. The pharmacokinetics and safety of alternative dosing regimens of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) during TB co-treatment need to be better understood. 5. Further research is required to determine the outcomes of treating co-infections of TB and histoplasmosis in individuals living with HIV.
